sample_data.method: Seeded on start from data/P10_prepaid_meter_public.json, with validated JSON file upload for published or unpublished judge fixtures.
sample_data.reset_instructions: Click 'Restore samples' after loading a judge JSON file, or refresh the page before any file has been loaded. Select PUB-01 for the documented default evidence.

problem_solving_method: Model the prepaid meter as a deterministic daily money ledger. Process start-of-day recharges and the month's first-recharge fixed charges, split each day's units progressively across calendar-month slab boundaries, add 5% VAT to energy only, and preserve a trace for every day. Reuse the same tariff primitive for balance reconstruction, run-out forecasting, target-date top-ups and both habit simulations so the comparison cannot fabricate an energy-rate saving.

R1.evidence: The home page loads all 25 official v2.1 cases from data/P10_prepaid_meter_public.json, defaults to PUB-01 with 181 consecutive readings, identifies its light and heavy months and ৳4,300 late-May recharge, and accepts validated same-shape JSON through 'Load judge JSON'. Validation is in lib/fixture.ts.

R2.evidence: The 'Daily money trail' shows the reconstructed closing-balance line, all recharge markers, a day scrubber and monthly audit table. Exact tariff, VAT and first-recharge logic is in lib/tariff.ts and lib/ledger.ts; the chart is components/balance-chart.tsx.

R3.evidence: The hero shows the run-out date at usual daily use. The 'How much should we recharge?' date input updates the top-up immediately and reconciles base energy, higher-slab uplift, fixed charges, VAT and current balance. See forecastRunOut and calculateTargetRecharge in lib/ledger.ts.

R4.evidence: The 'Recharge timing, honestly compared' section runs both policies over the case's exact three months and reports consumed cost separately from deposits. It visibly proves zero energy-cost difference. All 25 public cases pass that invariant in tests/tariff.test.ts.

major_design_decisions: Use a local deterministic ledger instead of Supabase or ML so every judged answer works offline and is auditable.
Use integer paisa and round each day's 5% energy VAT to the nearest paisa to avoid floating-point money drift.
Split usage progressively across slab boundaries and reset the counter only on calendar-month changes.
Accept same-shape JSON fixtures and validate consecutive dates, money fields and comparison months before calculation.
Use a custom SVG balance chart and native controls to avoid an unnecessary charting dependency.
known_limitations: Imported judge fixtures last for the current browser session only; the app intentionally has no account or server persistence.
Future usage follows the case's stated usual_daily_units as a constant because the problem supplies that value and does not request a probabilistic forecast.
The first public build supports seeded cases and JSON file upload, not manual row-by-row entry.

ai_tools_used.how_output_was_verified: Pure-domain tests cover all 25 public fixtures, every slab boundary, monthly fixed charges, target reconciliation and the R-16 energy-cost invariant. The team also runs TypeScript checking, a production Next.js build and desktop/mobile browser QA.
